# Architecture

## Modules

| Module       | What it is                                                                  |
|--------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `:shared`    | Kotlin Multiplatform library (Android + iOS targets). All the app's code.  |
| `:androidApp`| The Android application: `MainActivity` builds the root component and shows it. |

The iOS targets exist so that `commonMain` cannot use `java.*` or `android.*`. Building an iOS
app is not needed.

## Packages of `:shared`

```text
com.fxrates
├── core/        ← helpers with no knowledge of features
│   ├── format/  ← NumberFormatter: the only place numbers become strings
│   ├── money/   ← arithmetic on rates (RateChangeCalculator)
│   └── utils/   ← Resource, resourceFlow, String.Empty
├── domain/      ← pure models and repository interfaces; no Ktor, no Compose, no DTOs
│   ├── model/
│   └── repository/
├── data/        ← everything that talks to the outside world
│   ├── remote/  ← FrankfurterApi (Ktor), DTOs, the HTTP client
│   └── repository/ ← repository implementations and DTO → domain converters
├── feature/<feature>/<screen>/ ← screens, see screen.md
├── root/        ← the navigation stack of the app
├── ui/          ← AppTheme, Strings
└── di/          ← AppComponent: the kotlin-inject graph
```

Dependencies point one way: `feature → domain ← data`. A screen sees `domain` interfaces and
models only — never a DTO, never `FrankfurterApi`, never `HttpClient`.

## Data

- The API is [Frankfurter](https://frankfurter.dev) (`https://api.frankfurter.dev/v1/`), ECB
  reference rates, no key. Rates exist for business days only: weekends and holidays have no
  entry, so "the last 30 days" is fewer than 30 points.
- An endpoint is a method of `FrankfurterApi` returning a DTO from `data/remote/dto`.
- A DTO is converted into a domain model in `data/repository/*Converter`, never in the screen.
- Numbers from the API become `BigDecimal` (`com.ionspin.kotlin.bignum`) in the converter,
  through the string form, so the decimal digits the API sent are kept.
- A repository is an interface in `domain/repository` and an `*Impl` in `data/repository`, bound
  in `AppComponent`. A new read for an existing data source is a new method on the existing
  repository, not a new repository.

## Dependency injection

kotlin-inject. A class with an `@Inject` constructor needs no registration. An interface is
bound in `di/AppComponent.kt` with a `@Provides fun Impl.bindX(): X = this`. Long-lived objects
(the HTTP client, repositories) are `@AppScope`.

A Decompose component is created through an `@AssistedFactory`: the `ComponentContext`, the
screen arguments and the `Callbacks` are `@Assisted`, everything else is injected.
# Anatomy of a screen

Reference implementation: `feature/rates/list/`.

## Files

```text
feature/<feature>/<screen>/
├── mvi/
│   ├── XxxStore.kt          ← Intent / Action / Message / Label / State
│   ├── XxxReducer.kt        ← pure State.reduce(Message)
│   ├── XxxExecutor.kt       ← side effects
│   └── XxxStoreFactory.kt   ← assembles the Store, starts loading via a Bootstrapper
├── model/                   ← @Immutable UI models (rows, sections)
├── XxxUiState.kt            ← @Immutable state the composables draw
├── XxxUiStateConverter.kt   ← Store.State → UiState
├── XxxUiComponent.kt        ← abstract contract + Default (Factory, Callbacks)
├── XxxUiContent.kt          ← composables
└── XxxUiStatePreviewProvider.kt ← preview states
```

## Data flow

```text
Compose ─click─► UiComponent ─accept(Intent)─► Executor ─forward(Action)─► Executor ─► Repository
                                                   │                          │
                                              publish(Label)           dispatch(Message)
                                                   ▼                          ▼
                                     UiComponent → Callbacks        Reducer → State
                                                                              ▼
                                                     UiStateConverter → UiState → Compose
```

## MVI rules

- `Intent`, `Action`, `Message`, `Label` are nested `sealed class`es of the Store.
- **`State` holds domain models**, wrapped in `Resource` when they are loaded. No strings for
  display, no Compose types.
- **The Reducer is pure**: an expression-body `when` over every `Message`, only `copy(...)`.
- **`executeIntent` only does `dispatch`, `publish` and `forward`.** It may read `state()`.
- **Every side effect starts in `executeAction`**, and `executeAction` never reads `state()`: the
  Action carries everything it needs.
- A repository call is always `resourceFlow { repository.x() }.onEach { dispatch(...) }.launchIn(scope)`
  — never a bare `scope.launch { }` and never `runCatching`.
- A handler is named after its Intent/Action: `Action.LoadRates` → `loadRates(action)`. No
  `handle…`, `process…`, `do…`.
- Initial loading goes through `SimpleBootstrapper(Action.Load…)` in the factory.

## UiState and the converter

- `UiState` contains only what the screen draws, already formatted: strings, flags, UI models.
- All formatting and derived values are computed in `XxxUiStateConverter` through
  `NumberFormatter` and `core/money`. A composable never formats or calculates.
- A loading / error / content alternative is a sealed `Content` inside the `UiState`.

## UiComponent

- `abstract class XxxUiComponent` exposes `state: StateFlow<XxxUiState>` and one function per
  user action. The composable only knows this contract.
- `XxxUiComponentDefault` owns the Store, maps `states` through the converter and turns `Label`s
  into `Callbacks` calls.

## Navigation

- The stack lives in `root/RootUiComponent.kt`: a `@Serializable sealed class Config` and a
  `Child` per screen.
- **A screen does not navigate.** It publishes a `Label`, its component calls a `Callbacks`
  method, and the root pushes a `Config`.
- **A `Config` carries identifiers, not models** (`code`, `base`), so it survives process death.
  The destination screen loads what it needs itself.
- Back is handled by the stack (`handleBackButton = true`); a screen's own back button calls a
  `Callbacks` method, and the root pops.

## Tests

Every screen has at least:

- a **Store test** — a real Store from `XxxStoreFactory` with `DefaultStoreFactory()` and a fake
  repository; asserts `store.state` and the published labels after intents;
- a **UiStateConverter test** — State in, UiState out; this is where the formatted strings and
  the edge cases (empty data, nulls, zero) are checked.

See `RatesListStoreTest` and `RatesListUiStateConverterTest`.
# Code conventions

## Kotlin

- **No `it` in lambdas.** Name the parameter (`{ rate -> rate.code }`) or use a reference
  (`map(CurrencyRate::code)`). Names are full words: `rate`, not `r`.
- **Lambda properties and `invoke` operators are called explicitly:** `onClick.invoke()`.
- **`String.Empty`** (`core/utils`) instead of `""` in State, UiState and converters.
- **`sealed class`**, not `sealed interface`, for closed hierarchies.
- **Braces in a `when` are uniform:** if one branch is a block, all are.
- **Expression body** only when the body fits on one line; a trailing lambda
  (`= Column { … }`, `= when (x) { … }`) is fine.
- Constants: a top-level `const val` is `UpperCamelCase`; inside an `object` or a
  `companion object` it is `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE`.
- Lines are at most 120 characters. An empty line after the opening `{` and before the closing
  `}` of a class body.
- KDoc only where it says something the signature does not: a unit, why a value is nullable, an
  invariant. Comments are in English.

## Money and numbers

- **Rates and everything derived from them are `BigDecimal`** (`com.ionspin.kotlin.bignum`).
  `Double` and `Float` are not used for rates, amounts or their changes: binary floating point
  cannot represent most decimal fractions.
- Numbers become strings only through `core/format/NumberFormatter`. No `toString()` of a
  number in UI code, no hand-made rounding.
- A percent is shown with two decimals and an explicit sign (`+1.23%`, `-0.50%`); a value that
  rounds to zero has no sign (`0.00%`).

## Compose

- Spacing comes from `AppTheme.spacing`, semantic colours (up / down / neutral) from
  `AppTheme.colors`, text styles from `MaterialTheme.typography`. No literal `dp` and no literal
  `Color` in a screen.
- User-facing strings are in `ui/Strings.kt`, never inline in a composable.
- The public composable takes the component; it collects the state and delegates to a private
  stateless overload that takes `UiState` and lambdas. Previews render the stateless overload
  with states from the `PreviewParameterProvider`.
- Callbacks are named after the event: `onCurrencyClick`, `onRefresh`, `onBack`.

## Tests

- kotest, `FunSpec`, in `shared/src/commonTest`. Matchers from `io.kotest.matchers`.
- Fakes, not mocks: a hand-written `Fake…Repository` in `commonTest/.../testing`.
- Code that runs on `Dispatchers.Main` gets `Dispatchers.setMain(...)` in `beforeSpec` and
  `resetMain()` in `afterSpec`.
- A test name says the behaviour, not the method: `"a failed load ends in an error"`.
# Commands

All modules except `:androidApp` are Kotlin Multiplatform, so the Android task names differ
from a plain Android project: there is no `testDebugUnitTest` in `:shared`.

| What                         | Command                                         |
|------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------|
| Compile the shared code      | `./gradlew :shared:compileAndroidMain`          |
| Unit tests                   | `./gradlew :shared:testAndroidHostTest`         |
| Static analysis              | `./gradlew detekt`                              |
| Build the APK                | `./gradlew :androidApp:assembleDebug`           |
| Install on a device/emulator | `./gradlew :androidApp:installDebug`            |

Test reports: `shared/build/reports/tests/testAndroidHostTest/index.html`.
Detekt report: `shared/build/reports/detekt/detekt.html`.

## Before calling a change done

1. `./gradlew :shared:testAndroidHostTest detekt :androidApp:assembleDebug` is green.
2. The app was launched and the changed screen was looked at, including the loading and error
   states (airplane mode is enough for the error).
# Currency detail screen

## Current code

- `RatesListExecutor` already publishes `Label.OpenCurrency(base, code)` when a row is tapped, and `RatesListUiComponentDefault` forwards it. `RootUiComponentDefault.RatesListCallbacks.onOpenCurrency` is a stub. The root stack already handles system Back.
- `FrankfurterApi.getTimeSeries` accepts inclusive dates. `RatesRepositoryImpl` already receives a `Clock` and uses UTC for its list lookback. `RatesConverter.toLatestRates` produces a latest-rate snapshot from the last two dates, so detail needs its own conversion of the same time-series DTO.
- `RateChangeCalculator` checks the previous rate for zero but divides by the current rate using `Double`. `NumberFormatter.formatSignedPercent` converts that `Double` back to `BigDecimal`. The list converter tests check the signs without checking the percentage values.

## Ordered implementation

1. **Correct shared arithmetic and verify RatesList.** In `RateChange.kt`, return a `RateChange` with `absolute: BigDecimal` and `percent: BigDecimal?`. Compute `absolute = current − previous` and calculate the percentage as `(absolute × 100) / previous` using `BigDecimal.divide` with 34 significant digits and half-away-from-zero rounding so recurring quotients are supported. For a zero previous rate, retain the absolute change and leave the percentage unavailable. Update `NumberFormatter.formatSignedPercent` to take `BigDecimal` directly. Keep four decimals for absolute changes and two for percentages, with the sign determined after rounding. Rounded zero displays as `0.0000` or `0.00%`. Update `RatesListUiStateConverter` to format the nullable percentage and retain its neutral treatment when a comparison is unavailable. Verify in `RateChangeCalculatorTest`, `NumberFormatterTest`, and `RatesListUiStateConverterTest`. Include `100 → 125` yielding `+25.00%`, `125 → 100` yielding `-20.00%`, `3 → 4` yielding `+33.33%`, and `100 → 0` yielding `-100.00%`. Check that a missing previous quote still gives the list row no percentage.

2. **Add the history read.** Add `RateObservation(date: LocalDate, rate: BigDecimal)` in `domain/model` and `suspend fun getRateHistory(base: String, code: String): List<RateObservation>` to `RatesRepository`. In `RatesRepositoryImpl`, capture `end = clock.todayIn(TimeZone.UTC)` once per request and use `start = end.minus(DatePeriod(days = 29))`. Call `FrankfurterApi.getTimeSeries(base, start, end)` once. Add `RatesConverter.toRateHistory` to keep only dates inside the inclusive window with a rate for `code`, reuse the existing decimal conversion, and sort newest first. The first retained row supplies the latest quote and its date. The last retained row supplies the earliest quote. Skip weekends, holidays, and dates missing the selected code. Verify with `RatesConverterTest` and a fixed-clock `RatesRepositoryImplTest` using the existing Ktor `MockEngine`. For UTC November 12, 2026, assert the request is `2026-10-14..2026-11-12` with the selected base. Cover unsorted dates, gaps, out-of-window rows, a missing code on the newest response date, a single retained quote, and zero retained quotes.

3. **Build the detail Store.** Under `feature/rates/detail/mvi`, mirror `RatesList` with `CurrencyDetailStore`, `CurrencyDetailStoreFactory`, `CurrencyDetailExecutor`, and `CurrencyDetailReducer`. State holds `base`, `code`, and `Resource<List<RateObservation>>`, initially `Loading`. The factory uses `SimpleBootstrapper(Action.LoadHistory(base, code))`. `Intent.OnRetry` forwards that action from the error state and `Intent.OnBack` publishes `Label.GoBack`. Keep repository effects in `executeAction`, with both identifiers on the action and no state reads. Use `resourceFlow { repository.getRateHistory(...) }.onEach { history -> dispatch(Message.UpdateHistory(history)) }.launchIn(scope)`. The reducer only copies the history resource. Extend `FakeRatesRepository` with a configurable history result and recorded `(base, code)` requests. In `CurrencyDetailStoreTest`, use a real Store from `DefaultStoreFactory` and the list tests’ Main-dispatcher setup. Verify `Loading → Data` with one request, `Error → Loading → Data` after retry with the same pair, empty history as `Data(emptyList())`, and `OnBack` emitting `GoBack`. Use a suspended fake response to observe loading deterministically.

4. **Render the detail screen.** Add `CurrencyDetailUiState`, `CurrencyDetailUiStateConverter`, `CurrencyDetailUiComponent` and its `Default`, `CurrencyDetailUiContent`, an immutable history row model, and `CurrencyDetailUiStatePreviewProvider`. The component owns and disposes the Store with its lifecycle, maps `states` to `StateFlow`, and forwards `GoBack` through `Callbacks.onBack()`. The converter prepares the pair heading, latest quote and date, dated history rows, and period changes using the shared calculator and formatter. The composable collects state and delegates to a private stateless overload. Keep Back visible in every state, show a spinner during loading, reuse `Strings.ERROR_TITLE` and `Strings.RETRY` for failures, and render history in a newest-first `LazyColumn` keyed by date. Use `AppTheme`, Material typography, and `ui/Strings.kt`. Verify in `CurrencyDetailUiStateConverterTest` that loading and error map correctly, empty data displays a no-rates message, one quote displays the latest and one row with period change unavailable, and two or more quotes compare the endpoints. Assert signed pairs such as `+25.0000` and `+25.00%`, and `-25.0000` and `-20.00%`. Also assert unsigned zero for unchanged and tiny changes of either sign, and absolute-only output for a zero earliest rate.

5. **Wire root navigation and verify end to end.** Add serializable `Config.CurrencyDetail(base, code)` and `Child.CurrencyDetail` in `RootUiComponent`. Push the config from `RatesListCallbacks.onOpenCurrency`, create the child through `CurrencyDetailUiComponentDefault.Factory`, and pop from the detail callback. Keep `handleBackButton = true` for system Back. The `@AssistedFactory` takes `ComponentContext`, `base`, `code`, and `Callbacks`. Constructor injection supplies the detail Store factory and converter, and the Store factory uses the existing `AppComponent` providers for `StoreFactory` and `RatesRepository`. Add the child branch to `RootUiContent`. Keep application code in `shared/src/commonMain` and Kotest tests in `shared/src/commonTest`, with no new dependencies. Run `./gradlew :shared:testAndroidHostTest detekt :androidApp:assembleDebug`, then install with `./gradlew :androidApp:installDebug`. On a device or emulator, open a currency from the list on a throttled connection and check loading, the pair and dated latest quote, newest-first history, and signed changes. Use the screen’s Back button, take the device offline while the list is visible, open detail again, check the error, restore connectivity, and verify Retry loads the same pair. Use system Back to return to the list.

## Assumptions and submission

- **Defaults for decisions left open by `TASK.md`.** The period is 30 UTC calendar dates including today. The current quote is the newest available observation for the pair inside that window. A successful response with no usable quotes shows an empty state. Request failures show Retry. One quote is enough to display a rate, and two are needed to calculate change. Dates use ISO format and the heading uses currency codes.
- **Commit sequence.** Commit the shared percentage fix and regression tests, then the history repository read and data tests, then the detail screen and navigation with Store and converter tests, then the submission notes and logs. Use small English commits and preserve the history without squash or force-push.
- **Submission checklist.** Confirm the submission repository was created using GitHub’s **Use this template** and grant `karasvladimir` access if it is private. Include complete, unedited exports of all AI sessions, including planning and implementation, in `ai-logs/`. Keep secrets out of sessions and check the exports before committing. If the logs are too large for Git, attach the complete archive to the submission email. Write a root `SOLUTION.md` of at most half a page after implementation, recording the tools and models actually used, how project context was provided, any AI mistakes and how they were caught, and what was corrected by hand. Submit the repository link.
